key_insight: The paper argues that safety-critical autonomous systems need coordination guarantees enforced in hardware, not just software, so that timing, authorization, and interaction rules remain deterministic under uncertainty.
engineering_relevance: For real-time autonomous platforms, FPGA-based coordination can provide bounded latency and verifiable semantic control while leaving higher-level reasoning to software.
method: Build on the Topic-Based Communication Space Petri Net (TB-CSPN) framework.
Map selected coordination semantics to FPGA primitives.
Keep semantic reasoning in software while enforcing synchronization, gating, and authorization in hardware.
evidence_signal: The abstract presents a conceptual architecture and motivation, but does not report experimental results, benchmarks, or quantitative evaluation.
watch_item: A key implementation concern is the complexity of correctly translating coordination semantics into FPGA logic without reducing flexibility or introducing verification overhead.
paper_title: Hardware-Enforced Semantic Coordination for Safety-Critical Real-Time Autonomous Systems
